text: The Hurewicz theorem (in the simply-connected case) says: if X is (n-1)-connected (πₖ(X)=0 for k<n), then:
choices: Hₙ(X) ≅ πₙ(X) (first non-trivial homology equals first non-trivial homotopy group)
explanation: Hurewicz: if πₖ(X)=0 for k<n, then Hₖ(X)=0 for 0<k<n and Hₙ(X)≅πₙ(X). This bridges homotopy and homology in the first non-trivial dimension.
